notice: Synthetic institutional policies written for the Fluid demo. Not real guidance.

policies.title: Acute pain management with opioids, adults
policies.orderGuidance: Order through the 'Acute pain, opioid-naive adult' order set (OS-114, synthetic), which presents the institution's starting options for the clinician to select.
basis: Use the lowest effective starting option in the order set and reassess pain and sedation scores before any repeat dose.
Pharmacy verifies the first dose against renal function, hepatic function, and interacting sedatives.
Co-prescribe naloxone with any scheduled or as-needed opioid.

policies.title: Acute pain management with opioids, pediatrics
policies.orderGuidance: Order through the 'Pediatric acute pain' order set (OS-207, synthetic); a pediatric pharmacist verifies every opioid order.
basis: Pediatric opioid orders require a current weight documented in the chart within the encounter.
Continuous pulse oximetry is required for the first opioid dose and after any escalation.
Children under one year are managed only with the Pediatric Pain Service consult.

policies.title: Opioid use in adults 65 and older
policies.orderGuidance: Use the older-adult modifier in OS-114 (synthetic), which preselects the reduced starting options.
basis: Older adults start at the reduced options in the order set because of higher sedation and fall risk.
Screen for delirium and constipation daily while an opioid is active.

policies.title: Opioids in renal impairment
policies.orderGuidance: Pharmacy consult is required before the first opioid dose when eGFR is in the stage 4 range (synthetic rule).
basis: Active metabolites accumulate in advanced kidney disease; the pharmacy consult selects the agent and interval.
Avoid scheduled dosing until the pharmacy consult is complete.

policies.title: Use of decision support in clinical care
policies.orderGuidance: Decision support shows institutional policy and its basis; ordering decisions remain with the treating clinician.
basis: Clinical mode cites institutional policy so the clinician can review the basis independently.
Clinical mode never computes a patient-specific dose.
